Determining the "most valuable books in the world" usually falls into two categories: **priceless cultural artifacts** (many of which are locked away in national museums and never for sale) and **record-breaking auction titans**.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_books_and_manuscripts)

Rather than an arbitrary 100-item ledger, the world's most valuable printed books and manuscripts are defined by historical weight, extreme rarity, and multi-million-dollar sales.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_books_and_manuscripts)

### The All-Time Most Expensive Books & Manuscripts Sold at Auction

These works have shattered records through private sales or public auctions:

1. **Codex Leicester** — *Leonardo da Vinci* ($66.9 Million)
	- *What it is:* Da Vinci’s famous 72-page scientific journal filled with handwritten notes and sketches on astronomy, water, and fossils. Purchased by Bill Gates in 1994.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_books_and_manuscripts)
2. **United States Constitution (First Printing)** ($51.3 Million)
	- *What it is:* One of only 11 known surviving official printings from the Constitutional Convention of 1787.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_books_and_manuscripts)
3. **Codex Sassoon** ($40.3 Million)
	- *What it is:* The earliest, most complete Hebrew Bible known to exist, dating from the late 9th or early 10th century.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_books_and_manuscripts)
4. **Bay Psalm Book** (~$14M to $19.6 Million)
	- *What it is:* The first book ever printed in British North America (1640).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_books_and_manuscripts)
5. **Gutenberg Bible** ($2.4M – $35+ Million estimated per copy)
	- *What it is:* The first major book printed using mass-produced movable metal type in the West (c. 1455). Fewer than 50 incomplete or complete copies survive.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_books_and_manuscripts)
6. **John James Audubon’s *The Birds of America*** ($8M – $17.1 Million per copy)
	- *What it is:* A colossal double-elephant folio featuring hand-colored, life-size prints of North American birds. Multiple copies have cleared the $1 million+ mark.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_books_and_manuscripts)
7. **William Shakespeare’s *First Folio*** ($10M – $12.4+ Million)
	- *What it is:* Titled *Mr. William Shakespeare's Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies* (1623), it is the primary source for 18 of Shakespeare's plays that would otherwise have been lost.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_books_and_manuscripts)

### Most Valuable Literary & 20th-Century First Editions

For collectors tracking market-rising fiction and modern classics (tracked heavily via rare-book indexes and houses like Stanley Gibbons):

- ***The Great Gatsby* by F. Scott Fitzgerald** (First edition with dust jacket can command upwards of $200,000–$250,000).
- ***The Hobbit* by J.R.R. Tolkien** (1937 first edition, first impression with original dust jacket).
- ***Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone* by J.K. Rowling** (1997 Bloomsbury hardback first impression—specifically the rare run of 500 copies where 300 went to libraries).
- ***Ulysses* by James Joyce** (1922 signed/limited first editions published by Shakespeare and Company in Paris).
- ***Action Comics #1* / *Superman #1*** (While comic books, they frequently top rare-document value charts, with prime grades fetching $6M–$9M+).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_books_and_manuscripts)
